headline: New law requires federal courts to let victims of the 1988 Lockerbie bombing watch the related criminal trial remotely.
what_it_does: Federal courts must offer remote access to the criminal proceedings against Abu Agila Mohammed Mas'ud Kheir Al-Marimi, who is charged in the 1988 bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland. The same rule applies to any co-conspirator later charged and prosecuted in federal court for crimes tied to the bombing. This lets victims follow the case without traveling to the courthouse.

who_it_affects.group: Victims of the Pan Am Flight 103 bombing
who_it_affects.how: They gain the ability to watch or listen to the related federal criminal court proceedings remotely.

who_it_affects.group: Federal courts handling the Lockerbie bombing case
who_it_affects.how: They must set up and provide remote access to these specific criminal proceedings.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 26, 2024; the summary does not list a separate start date.
